sections.category: Wiz's GhostApproval research shows a symlink planted in a repository can redirect an AI coding agent's file write onto a victim's SSH keys, hitting six major assistants including Claude Code, Cursor, and Amazon Q

bullets.body: Wiz Research publicly disclosed GhostApproval on July 8, a trust-boundary flaw that turns a decades-old filesystem feature — the symbolic link — into a repository-borne attack on AI coding assistants. A malicious repo ships a file with an innocuous name such as project_settings.json that is actually a symlink pointing at ~/.ssh/authorized_keys; when a developer asks the agent to set up the workspace or follow the README and approves what looks like a harmless config edit, the write lands on the SSH file instead, planting an attacker's key and granting passwordless remote access. The core failure is a consent bypass: the approval dialog shows only the benign filename, so the human okays an edit whose real target they never see resolve. Wiz reported it to six vendors — Amazon Q Developer, Anthropic's Claude Code, Augment, Cursor, Google Antigravity, and Windsurf. Amazon (CVE-2026-12958), Cursor (CVE-2026-50549), and Google Antigravity shipped fixes; Augment and Windsurf were still unpatched at disclosure; and Anthropic disputed that Claude Code's behavior is a bug, arguing a developer who trusts a directory and approves an edit owns that decision, placing it outside its threat model. The split verdict is the real story: the industry has not agreed whether silently following a symlink into a sensitive path on the user's behalf is the tool's vulnerability or the user's mistake.

sections.category: A Technical University of Munich benchmark, ThorArena, replays recorded human motion-and-force data in simulation and finds leading humanoid whole-body controllers degrade sharply once real contact forces enter the picture

bullets.body: Researchers at the Technical University of Munich published ThorArena on arXiv, a benchmark that stress-tests humanoid whole-body control under the deliberate, load-bearing physical contact that real human-robot co-working involves — not collision avoidance, but active force exchange. The team captured synchronized whole-body motion and hand forces from human operators wearing VR headsets, motion trackers, and 3D-printed force-sensing tools while performing six contact-rich chores — lifting and lowering a water container, pushing and pulling a chair, and co-carrying an object with a partner — then replayed those forces in simulation against representative control policies. Their metric, the Force-Aware Tracking Score (FATS), jointly grades tracking accuracy, robustness across force levels, control effort, and whether the robot stays upright to the end of the episode. The headline finding, echoed in independent coverage: force-informed evaluation exposes large performance gaps that stay invisible under conventional no-force testing, and the authors' own Thor2 policy was the only entry to hold near-perfect balance across all six tasks. The result lands as Figure, Agility, and Boston Dynamics push humanoids from pilots into factories and warehouses, where a person will inevitably lean on, push, or hand something to the robot — precisely the regime today's controllers handle worst.

sections.category: Micron lifts its US manufacturing commitment to $250 billion through 2035 and pours the first concrete at its Clay, New York memory megafab a quarter early, tying the expansion explicitly to AI-era demand for DRAM and HBM

bullets.body: Micron said on July 9 it is raising its planned US investment to more than $250 billion through 2035, a $50 billion increase over the $200 billion plan it set in mid-2025, and framed the bump squarely as a response to surging AI-era memory demand. The announcement coincided with the first concrete pour at its Clay, New York site — more than a quarter ahead of the original schedule — marking the shift from site preparation to vertical construction on what Micron says will become the largest semiconductor manufacturing site in US history. The company reiterated a goal of producing 40% of its DRAM on US soil. The raise underscores how memory has become the AI accelerator's binding constraint: HBM stacks and advanced DRAM are sold out well into the future, and it comes days after SK Hynix's record US listing earmarked proceeds for EUV-equipped capacity — two of the three big memory makers committing fresh capital to the same bottleneck in the same week.

sections.category: AI events to plan around now: AMD Advancing AI opens Moscone on July 22-23, then an August run of chip, security, and developer summits — Black Hat and DEF CON, the AI Risk Summit, Ai4, Hot Chips, and Anyscale's newly-dated Ray Summit on August 24-26

bullets.body: The nearest date on the calendar is AMD Advancing AI 2026 at San Francisco's Moscone West on July 22-23, where Lisa Su and partners are expected to detail the Instinct MI450 accelerator and Zen 6 EPYC "Venice" CPUs — free to attend in person and livestreamed, and the natural venue for AMD's answer to Blackwell. On the AI-chip track behind it, Hot Chips runs at Stanford on August 23-25 with the early-registration rate closing July 31, followed by the AI Infra Summit in Santa Clara on September 15-17. The AI-security track clusters in early-to-mid August: Black Hat USA (August 1-6) and DEF CON 34's AI Village in Las Vegas, SecurityWeek's AI Risk Summit at the Ritz-Carlton in Half Moon Bay on August 11-12, OWASP Global AppSec USA in San Francisco on November 5-6, and Zenity's AI Agent Security Summit series for teams working agent-hijack and MCP-layer defense. On the developer, data, and Bay Area track, Anyscale's Ray Summit now has firm dates — August 24-26 at the San Francisco Marriott Marquis (a training day plus two days on scaling LLM and reinforcement-learning workloads), the next AI Tinkerers San Francisco meetup runs in August in the usual working-demo format, Ai4 2026 fills The Venetian in Las Vegas on August 4-6, the ACM AI Leadership Summit runs August 30 to September 2 in Atlanta, The AI Conference returns to Pier 48 on September 29 to October 1, GitHub Universe is October 28-29, AWS re:Invent runs November 30 to December 4 in Las Vegas, and NeurIPS 2026 closes the year in December. Near-term actions: register for AMD Advancing AI before the July 22 open, lock the July 31 Hot Chips early rate, and book Black Hat plus the AI Risk Summit for the early-August security block.
